items.description: The converted build changes syntax, not what it does: the Replay's pod, as the `kubernetes` plugin prints it at the top of the console, matches a scripted Build-Main build's (containers, images, pull policies, users, resources, the inherited `kaniko` container, init container and volumes), and the same stages run in the same order, ending in the KubeCoderDeploy pin write.

items.description: The operator gives the verdict: migrate them all, or keep the J08 rule (declarative on `iac-controller`, scripted for pod pipelines). If "migrate all", the migration is a slice of its own.

items.description: `containerTemplates.podYaml(...)` is on JenkinsPipelineUtils' main: it renders the library sidecars a caller names, under the caller's container names, plus the caller's own containers, as one pod spec a declarative Kubernetes agent takes. Each sidecar's settings are written once, so the scripted describable and the YAML form cannot drift, and scripted consumers of `containerTemplates.*` see no change. `kc project test` proves the rendered output.
evidence: JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/containerTemplates.groovy:19,62 — `k8s` and `modern_app_toolchain` return `containerTemplate(...)` describables, which an `agent` block cannot take (library HEAD 276beff)

items.description: The library's self-test asserts the pure functions `cicd.applyPins`/`replacePin`/`plainSafe`, `helmCharts.resolveTrackingTag`, `notify.escape`, `utils.hasChanges`, and references every var so each compiles. Per ruling D1 it runs in the pre-push Maven gate (`kc project test`); no Jenkins job or Jenkinsfile is added for the library.
evidence: JenkinsPipelineUtils/.kubecoder/project.yaml — `root`'s test is `cexec java mvn -B -q -f tests/pom.xml test`
JenkinsPipelineUtils/tests/src/test/java/org/webathome/jenkinspipelineutils/LibraryCompileTest.java:69-76 — every vars/*.groovy is compiled through the CPS transform
JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/cicd.groovy:188,275,326 and vars/notify.groovy:31 — `applyPins`, `replacePin`, `plainSafe` and `escape` are `@NonCPS`, so callable directly from JUnit

items.area: R3 — J22 compile gate's version pin
items.description: The compile gate's `groovy-cps.version` pin no longer trails the controller: it is the controller's `workflow-cps` version, as `tests/pom.xml` says it is ("bumped when the controller's workflow-cps is upgraded").
`utils.hasChanges` is annotated `@NonCPS` and otherwise as it was, verified with the J22 self-test: called with `'.*'` it answers true, with a pattern that cannot match it answers false.
evidence: JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/utils.groovy:33-41 — `def hasChanges(pattern)` has no `@NonCPS`, reads `currentBuild.changeSets` and calls no step

items.description: One run of a caller verifies `hasChanges` after the library push: "`DockerImages/Jenkinsfile` and `Ansible/Jenkinsfile.iac-image`; either one's next build is the verification run."
items.owed_after: the next build of DockerImages/Jenkinsfile or Ansible/Jenkinsfile.iac-image after the library push

items.description: The dead library code is removed — `helmCharts.tools`/`toolsInstalled`, `resolveImageTag`, `containerTemplates.debian`, `containerTemplates.canon` — and the KitchenDisplay-only code stays (`helmCharts.ssh`/`rsync`, `containerTemplates.rsync` and `dockbuild`, `gitUtils.groovy`), as do `kubectl.waitForJob` and `readFileFromPod`. Verified with the J22 self-test (compiles every var).
evidence: No `Jenkinsfile*` under /work or /work/scratch, and no exported job config under /work/scratch/jenkins-config/xml, names the deleted helpers (grep, 2026-09-30)

items.description: The run pushes JenkinsPipelineUtils to main once its gates pass, so the library the operator's Replay loads carries `podYaml`; KubeCoder's converted Jenkinsfile is committed but not pushed by the run.
No library test coverage is lost: slice 027's compile test and its controls (syntax error, `synchronized` block, CPS-transformed body) and `TrackingTagTest` still run and pass in `kc project test`.
